visual.general_description: Four pretransplant abdominal CT panels showing liver/vascular and renal anatomy.
visual.detailed_description: A two-by-two grayscale montage is labelled a,b,c,d. The upper row contains axial liver and coronal abdominal views with white arrowheads or an arrow. The lower row contains two axial kidney-containing views, each with a broad white arrow. Bone and contrast-bright vessels are dense white; organ parenchyma and muscles are gray. There are no chart axes, numeric measurements or size calipers.

panels.general_description: Axial upper-abdominal CT with portal-region arrowheads.
panels.detailed_description: Upper-left view labelled a is an axial abdominal grayscale CT. A large irregularly contoured gray liver occupies the image left; spleen and stomach/bowel structures lie on the image right. Dense ribs and a posterior vertebra are visible. Three small white triangular arrowheads surround a central liver/portal vascular-region structure. Bright contrast-filled vascular branches and gray parenchyma are visible. No caliper or numerical size label is printed.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Pretransplant CT of the recipient who underwent DDLTPretransplant CT findings of the recipient who underwent DDLT. a) The thrombus of the right portal vein was observed (arrowheads). b) Splenomegaly and splenorenal shunt (arrow) were shown. c and d) The bilateral kidneys were atrophic (arrows).Abbreviations: CT, computed tomography; DDLT, deceased donor liver transplantation

The Child-Pugh score was 12, and the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score was 18. Preoperative CT findings (Figure 1) demonstrated a cirrhotic liver morphology without viable tumors. A thrombus was detected in the main trunk of the right portal vein (Figure 1a). Splenomegaly, a splenorenal shunt (Figure 1b), pleural effusion, and ascites were also observed. The bilateral kidneys were atrophic (Figure 1c, 1d), suggesting pre-existing chronic kidney disease. Considering the preoperative renal dysfunction due to hepatorenal syndrome, the patient was considered to have acute-on-chronic kidney disease.

A POD23-25:ATG1.5mg/kg box and POD26:liver biopsy arrow appear at upper left; three yellow arrows marked sepsis point near successive early/middle peaks. Middle row has pink open-diamond AST, red open-circle ALT and dark-blue open-square γ-GTP series, with an early sharp AST/ALT spike and later lower fluctuations; orange NAd bars, blue HSS100mg/50mg blocks and a green PSL bar are placed above the curves. Bottom row has dark-blue solid-circle BUN and light-blue solid-square sCre trends. The shared x label reads Post-Operative Day (POD), with50/100/150/200 ticks. Middle and bottom y axes have breaks/nonuniform ranges. No printed laboratory point values are present; doses and biopsy timing are printed.

On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient suddenly developed severe acidemia (arterial pH 7.139), oliguria, markedly elevated hepatic enzymes (aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 7,994 IU/L, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 3,960 IU/L), and coagulopathy (prothrombin time-international normalized ratio (PT-INR) 2.33) (Figure 2).
